title: Corned Beef & Cabbage
description: From the Food Charlatan: My absolute favorite recipe for corned beef and cabbage! This easy dinner is made in the in the oven, you can just set it and forget it! This method gives you the most tender and juicy corned beef you’ve ever had, cooked in 3 ½ to 4 hours. Serve it with Roasted Red Potatoes and Horseradish Sauce for the perfect St. Patrick’s Day meal or any other time of the year!
ingredients: 4 pounds corned beef brisket, with spice packet
1 ½ cups beef broth (water & 1/12 tsp Better Than Bullion)
6 cloves garlic, smashed and left whole
15-20 whole peppercorns, or fresh cracked pepper to taste
8-10 sprigs fresh thyme, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme
1+ handfuls of baby carrots, or whole ones, peeled and quartered (8-10 carrots)
1 large head green cabbage, sliced into wedges
1 batch Roasted Red Potatoes, (2 pounds red potatoes needed)
parsley and or chives , to garnish
directions: Heat a large oven-proof pan over medium high heat for at least 2 minutes. Open your package of corned beef and drain the brine into the sink. There is no need to rinse the corned beef. Save the spice packet if there is one.

Add 2 tablespoons oil to the hot pot; it should shimmer immediately. Swirl to coat, then add the drained corned beef. Sear for 2-4 minutes on one side until golden brown, then carefully flip with tongs and sear the other side for another 2-3 minutes.

With the corned beef, fat side down. Add the 1½ cups beef broth, along with 3 tablespoons whole grain mustard, and the onions, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, peppercorns, and spice packet. Still any little pieces stuck to the bottom of the pan.
After 2 hours, flip the corned beef over and add the carrots.
After another 1 hour, add the cabbage, and continue cooking for another 30-60 minutes, until the cabbage is softened the way you like and has absorbed some of the corned beef flavor.
Meanwhile, make a batch of Roasted Red Potatoes in the oven. Potatoes do not belong in the watery pot.
Serve with a mixture of mayo and mustard, or a horseradish sauce: mayo, sour cream, horseradish, lemon, and salt & pepper to taste.
